Sam: Quick heads-up — sampleapp hitting duplicate webhook callbacks after a 429 during token refresh. Root cause looks like client retried without idempotency + sticky session moved to different instance. Anyone seen sticky-session + token-rotate -> replay?

Maria: Hmm. Do you have a repro? Which SDK? Node or Python?

Sam: Node, latest devex branch. Repro steps: 1) hit /generate with long prompt 2) force token rotate (rotate endpoint) 3) immediately retry on 429 from server. Observed two webhook calls. Logs below.

Sam: logs:
```
[2024-05-12T15:12:03Z] req_id=aa11  ->  POST /v1/generate  200-ish start
[2024-05-12T15:12:05Z] req_id=aa11  <-  429 Too Many Requests (quota burst)
[2024-05-12T15:12:05Z] retry=1 for req_id=aa11 (client retry)
[2024-05-12T15:12:05Z] token_rotate: old=tokA new=tokB
[2024-05-12T15:12:06Z] req_id=aa11  ->  POST /v1/generate Authorization: Bearer tokB
[2024-05-12T15:12:07Z] webhook fired for req_id=aa11 (side-effect)
[2024-05-12T15:12:07Z] webhook fired for req_id=aa11 (duplicate)
```

Maria: If you don't set an Idempotency-Key, retries can be unsafe. SDK usually injects a logical op id for idempotency on HTTP APIs — maybe missing for streaming or long-poll flows. Can you paste the request headers?

Sam: headers:
```
Authorization: Bearer tokA
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: sampleapp/0.1.0
# no Idempotency-Key present
```

Jay: Two angles here: 1) App-level: attach an Idempotency-Key (UUID) per logical user operation so retries are de-duped server-side. 2) Infra-level: token-rotation + sticky-sessions race — if a request gets routed to a different instance mid-op the KV cache for prefix/kv may be missed and a retry will replay the request. Recommend exponential backoff + randomized jitter for 429s that happen during or immediately after token rotation.

Jay: Suggested backoff snippet (pseudocode):
```js
function nextDelay(attempt) {
  const base = 100; // ms
  const expo = Math.pow(2, attempt);
  const jitter = 0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5; // 50-100%
  return Math.round(base * expo * jitter);
}
// use attempt count from 0, cap attempts, and definitely respect Retry-After header if present
```

Maria: Also think about a "safe-replay window" for streaming: SDK should avoid full replays if partial outputs were already produced. Add a replay-guard header (X-Redwood-Replay-Guard: nonce) that server checks to decide whether it's safe to replay side-effects.

DevX Bot: Docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/retries — includes idempotency, X-Redwood-Replay-Guard, and 429 best practices. See section "token rotation races" for patterns.

Sam: Thanks — I'll prototype adding Idempotency-Key in the Node SDK and an opt-in "sticky-token" header to keep requests tied to a token session. Will run load test and reproduce on staging. @Jay can you share sampleapp patch? :pray:

Jay: Pushed branch: https://git.redwood/patches/123 — added idempotency and jitter by default, with an opt-out flag. Also added a small middleware that sets X-Redwood-Replay-Guard when a request starts.
